summary: Model updated for the ValidateUpdate rewrite (explicit enable height, height-dependent validation, per-height enable-height history). Prior harness rebased; 16 fresh traces validated. One finding: the update rejects an unchanged, already reached VoteExtensionsEnableHeight, halting the chain; the baseline accepts it.
validation_limits: Bounded BFS (heights <= 3-5, <= 3 crashes, 1 app rollback, finite enable-height domains) plus 30-minute random simulations; exhausted bounds are not a proof.
Runtime traces use in-memory stores and scripted ABCI apps; crashes are injected by a failing state Save or app Commit, not by process kill.
Extended-commit storage itself is not observed; veHist is read from the state-store params history.
The after-reached clause of UnchangedVEUpdateNotRejected rests on contested requirement evidence (the updated unit test expects the rejection).
Bug-confirmation (Part 4) controller was not invoked; MC-1 status reflects in-run reproduction against the updated and baseline trees.

findings.title: Unchanged, already reached VoteExtensionsEnableHeight is rejected, halting the chain
findings.cause: The rewritten ValidateUpdate dropped the unchanged-value acceptance; row 6 (updated <= h) rejects U == E once 0 < E <= h.
findings.trigger: After the enable height E is reached, FinalizeBlock returns ConsensusParamUpdates whose Abci subrecord repeats E (e.g. complete params via ToProto).
findings.consequence: ApplyBlock fails before Commit, consensus panics, and every restart re-executes and rejects the same block; all nodes halt at that height.

premises: The application may return a non-nil Abci subrecord equal to the current enable height after that height is reached.
ApplyBlock errors are fatal in consensus and handshake replay re-executes the same block deterministically.
